# Design decisions and the principle behind them {#sec-principled-decisions}

**Every architectural decision in ISLA is made by one rule: an accuracy
gain is not accepted when it is known to come from a violation of a
physical principle.** A surrogate for a boundary-value problem must depend
on the geometry, the boundary conditions and the physics, and on nothing
else. When a change improves the score by reading the mesher's cell pattern,
the sampling density, or a statistic of the drawn sample, the improvement is
a fit to the discretization. It will not survive a different mesher, a
different sampling law, or a geometry the training set did not contain. This
appendix is the ledger of every decision of that kind: the alternative it
rejected, what the alternative would have bought on the in-distribution
metric, what it consumed that the physics does not provide, and the evidence.
It exists so that the paper on ISLA can say *why* the architecture is what it
is, and so that the position is stated plainly for others. A program that
wants highly generalizable physics surrogates must be willing to leave
measured accuracy on the table when that accuracy is known to be
non-physical.^[Not everything that is measured counts, and not everything
that counts can be measured. The aphorism is William Bruce Cameron's
(*Informal Sociology*, 1963); it is often misattributed to Einstein.]

```{python}
#| label: setup-design
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
```

## Names, symbols and colors {#sec-key}

**Every thing in this book has one name and every architecture one
color.** The names below are canonical. Their definitions are in the
chapters cited.

| Name | What it is | Where defined |
|---|---|---|
| **ISLA** | the model as shipped, named without qualifier: the relative frame, the RMS-pairwise-distance length unit, cosine routing, the class defaults | @sec-isla, @sec-using-config |
| **ablation**, **diagnostic** | a configuration measured only to price a design choice (weights-off, raw coordinates, linear routing); never adopted | @sec-principled-ledger |
| **GeoTransolver**, **Transolver**, **GeoTransolver-volume** | the public slice-attention baselines, named without qualifier and never modified. "GeoTransolver + ISLA's *feature* (ablation)" is a baseline with one of ISLA's features added to isolate an effect; it is not a variant of the public model | @sec-baselines |
| **DrivAerML Surface task**, **DrivAerML Volume task** | the two tasks on the car dataset: surface pressure and wall shear at the boundary cells; pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity at interior queries from the boundary alone | @sec-datasets |
| **HiLiftAeroML, the $n$-wing rung** | the wing dataset, and one training-set size on its data-efficiency ladder ("the 35-wing rung") | @sec-datasets, @sec-data-efficiency |
| **AirfRANS interior task** | the airfoil dataset's boundary-to-interior task | @sec-datasets |
| **global vector inputs**, **global scalar inputs** | the problem's global conditions: $K$ unit directions $\hat g_k$ and $S$ scalars $\sigma$; on the benchmark instances $K = 1$, the far-field direction, and $S \in \{0, 1\}$ | @sec-pde-theory, @sec-isla-inputs |
| **measure weight** $w_i$ | the surface area a sampled cell stands for; the quadrature weight of every sum in the model | @sec-isla-quadrature |
| **relative frame** | ISLA's construction of position: no center, positions used only as differences to anchors, the measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the sample as length unit | @sec-isla-frame |
| **slice**, **anchor** | a soft group of tokens, and its measure-weighted mean position and normal | @sec-isla-slices |
| **relational invariants** | the scalars that describe a token relative to an anchor | @sec-isla-relational |
| **contract** | a structural property asserted to roundoff in float64 as a unit test | @sec-fidelity-columns, @sec-isla-contracts |
| **the two invariances** | rigid-motion equivariance (a contract) and discretization consistency (an acceptance criterion) | @sec-invariances |
| **the four sampling draws** | uniform over cells, stratified, 10:1 front/back bias, area-proportional | @sec-sampling-laws |
| **area-weighted relative L2**, **float32 instrument** | the metric and the precision every reported number is scored at | @sec-metrics |
| **the reporting protocol** | 200,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, each architecture at its own best learning rate, two seeds | @sec-protocol |

Two conventions hold in every table and figure. **A ratio between
architectures is baseline error divided by ISLA error**, so a value above
one favors ISLA. **Every error is the area-weighted relative L2 of
@sec-metrics, scored in float32** on the final-epoch checkpoint. A few
within-architecture comparisons are scored in bfloat16, and their captions
say so. No bfloat16 number is compared across architectures.

## The criterion {#sec-principled-criterion}

**The operational form of the principle is discretization consistency,
stated and argued once in @sec-discretization-centerpiece: a prediction
that converges to one field under refinement and to the same field under
two sampling laws, tested by the consistency benchmark and its
training-law twin rather than by any single accuracy number.** The program
asks two questions of every proposed change, before and after it is
measured. *Why should this work*, in mechanistic terms? And would a
practitioner of classical CFD look at the construction without objecting
to what it consumes? Changes that cannot answer both are run, when they
are run at all, as ablations, and are labeled so wherever they appear. The
same two questions are the reason ISLA has one configuration. The
weights-off ablation is not adopted on the rungs where it scores better,
and no frame that centers on a statistic of the sample is in the class
(@sec-principled-ledger).

## The ledger {#sec-principled-ledger}


**Each row names the decision as it stands in ISLA, the alternative it
rejected, and what the alternative would have cost the physics.** "What it
would have bought" is the alternative's gain on the in-distribution
surface-pressure metric (float32, seed means) where it had one, with the
cell budget it was measured at; "what it reads" is the non-physical quantity
the gain came from; the evidence column points to the chapter or notebook
entry that carries the numbers and their artifacts. Five rows are decisions
of protocol, code or program rather than of architecture; each says so.
Where the alternative's gain was measured only on a configuration that is
no longer in the class, or only below the reporting protocol, the gain
column says "not re-measured" and the row stands on its principle.

| Decision | Rejected alternative | What it would have bought | What it reads that the physics does not provide | Evidence | Principle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Measure weights in the routing softmax | Unweighted routing (the weights-off ablation) | A gain on the small wing rungs; not re-measured | The number of cells the mesher placed in a region. Under area-proportional sampling the ablation's error rises above that of predicting zero; on the wings its advantage is flat in cell count, the signature of mesh-pattern content | @sec-limits-mechanism, @sec-consistency-bench, @sec-nb-bench-verdict, @sec-nb-overfit-routing-probe | A slice aggregate is an integral, not a point population |
| The origin-free frame: positions enter only as differences against anchors | A frame centered on the plain mean of the sampled points | Nothing on DrivAerML; a price on the wing rungs where validation geometries recur and at the fixed angle; not re-measured | The mesher's refinement pattern, through the plain mean's offset from the geometric centroid: under a sampling-density bias the centered frame degrades many-fold, and an exact full-geometry frame with every positional seed pays *more* than the origin-free construction, so the price is the pattern, not positional information | @sec-nb-frame-full-verdict, @sec-nb-frame-full-fixed-angle-verdict, @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-verdict | No statistic of the sample in the frame |
| The origin-free frame | A similarity gauge: measure-weighted centroid and RMS radius estimated from the sample | A price where validation geometries recur (35 and 210 wing cases); within seed noise on DrivAerML at 435 cars, so the price of not being told the body's center is inside seed noise; not re-measured | An absolute position on a wing that recurs between training and deployment. An estimated frame is a sample statistic even when it is consistent under refinement; the gain is a fit to a fixed fleet of shapes | @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-verdict, @sec-nb-relframe-verdict, @sec-nb-sgref-verdict | Built for the shapes not yet seen |
| Length unit $L$ from the measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the sample (the only length unit the class has) | A constant `reference_length` per dataset; the total-measure unit $L \equiv (\sum_i w_i)^{1/2}$ | Nothing: the per-dataset constant pays more at the fixed angle than the total-measure unit, and the RMS pairwise distance is within seed noise of the total-measure unit at 435 cars at the reporting protocol | The constant encodes the fleet's size by hand. The total-measure unit is an integral of the geometry and consistent under Horvitz–Thompson weights, but it is not center-free in the sense the RMS distance is, and it diverges on boundaries whose measure grows under refinement where the pairwise distance converges | @sec-nb-lenrms-verdict, @sec-nb-lenrms-200k, @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-verdict, @sec-nb-frame-full-fixed-angle-verdict | Length from the geometry, not from a table |

| The reporting protocol: 200,000 sampled cells per case, each architecture at its own best learning rate (a protocol decision) | Reporting at the exploration budget of 10,000 cells, or every architecture at one shared rate | Reporting at 10,000 cells would have reported a full-data ordering on DrivAerML that the count noise of a 10,000-cell draw produces and that 200,000 cells removes; a shared rate of 1e-3 would have understated GeoTransolver on every DrivAerML rung, most at the smallest, where its better rate is 3e-3 | A budget below the one the recipe trains at, and a rate that favors whichever architecture it was tuned on. At 200,000 cells and each model's better rate the reference configuration leads GeoTransolver-256 by 7% at full data on the cars and ties the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512, and the wing deficit is unchanged from the smaller budget, so the protocol changes no ordering it does not have to (@sec-surface) | @sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-prereg, @sec-nb-proto200k-verdict, @sec-scoreboard-200k | Report where you train, at each model's best |
| Every input and output is a named field of declared tensor rank; inputs enter through O(3)-invariants against the token's own directions, outputs leave through tensor products of the token's basis (a code decision) | Counted, typed channels (`out_scalars`, `out_vectors`, `n_boundary_scalars`, ...) with a flat concatenated output, and laboratory components of a boundary vector or a target tensor fed or read as separate scalars | Nothing: the aerodynamic configurations are unchanged parameter-for-parameter in the trunk, and the vector head loses only its two pseudovector basis elements | A laboratory component is an invariant only of a set that includes the frame, so component channels read the frame the physics does not provide (the Tensile2d clause, @sec-isla-heads); a flat output cannot say which channels form one tensor, so nothing downstream can hold them to a covariance. With the rank declared, a prescribed traction enters as $v \cdot \hat n$, $v \cdot \hat g_k$, $\lvert v \rvert$ and $v \cdot \hat\rho_{is}$ in every layer, and a stress leaves as a whole tensor whose components are a view | @sec-isla-inputs-rank, @sec-arch-head, @sec-nb-rank-spec-api | A component is a view of a tensor, never a channel |
| Present ISLA as a new architecture; leave GeoTransolver and Transolver unmodified | Back-port measure weighting and the origin-free frame into GeoTransolver and Transolver | A sampler-consistent GeoTransolver and Transolver at unchanged accuracy | Nothing non-physical; the released architectures are stable and in use, so their measure-consistent ablations locate a property and are never shipped modifications | @sec-nb-mwaw-verdict, @sec-nb-steelman-verdict, @sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines | Released models are not modified |
| Every input is a datum of the PDE problem: geometry, boundary data, material or flow parameters, body-force and load directions | The dataset's coordinate axes as global vectors (the laboratory frame on AirfRANS, the body axes on DrivAerML and the wings), which let the scalar heads produce frame components and let every token know its station in the canonical pose | 5 to 25% on fixed-pose datasets: 17% on AirfRANS interior pressure, 5% on DrivAerML Surface pressure, 11% on the 35-wing rung, 4 to 13% on DrivAerML Volume; component targets on the solids | The pose of the training set. A solver never takes these axes; rotating the problem rotates the solution, so the axes carry no information about the PDE and all of their gain is memorization of where things sit in the dataset's frame, the prior GeoTransolver has by construction and that the pose test (@sec-pose-contract) shows does not survive a change of pose | @sec-pose-prior, @sec-nb-ruling-dataset-frame-inputs | An input a solver would not need is not an input; accuracy bought with it does not count |

: The design-decision ledger. Every number is stated in the chapter or notebook entry the row points to and carries its artifact there. How to read this: a row records what the rejected alternative would have bought *in distribution* and what it would have read; it does not rank the decisions by size; a row whose gain column says "nothing" is a decision made on principle with no accuracy at stake, and a row that says "not re-measured" carries its principle without a current number. {#tbl-principled-ledger}

**Two rows deserve a sentence each, because they are the ones where the
principle cost the most.**

**The measure weights** are the clearest case. With them, a slice state is
a quadrature estimate of a surface integral. Without them it is a mean over
whichever points the mesher happened to place, and the network learns the
mesher. The price on the wings is real and understood. Part of it is the
estimator variance of a quadrature-weighted mean over a heavy-tailed draw of
cell areas, which shrinks with cell count and is nearly gone at 40,000 cells
on the cars. The rest is mesh-pattern content in the ablation, which does
not shrink and which collapses the moment the sampling law changes. An
accuracy table at one cell count cannot tell these apart. The consistency
benchmark can, and it decided.

**The frame** is the case where the trade is closest. Where the same
wings recur between training and validation, an estimated center and
scale buys accuracy against the origin-free construction. No such frame
is in the class, for three reasons. The never-seen-geometry rungs favor the
origin-free construction. On DrivAerML at 435 cars the price of
not being told the body's center is inside seed noise
(@sec-principled-ledger). And an estimated frame is a statistic of
the sample even when it is a consistent one. For a fixed fleet of shapes
an estimated frame is the better instrument. ISLA is built for the shapes
that have not been seen yet.

## What we would ask of the field {#sec-principled-ask}

**Three practices follow from the ledger, and none of them is expensive.**

- **Measure consistency, not only accuracy.** Score every model under at
  least two sampling laws and at more than one cell count, and report
  whether the answers converge to each other; then train under a second law
  and score on the first. A model that is 10% better at 10,000 cells and
  10x worse under a different sampler, or 8x worse when trained under a
  different law, has learned the mesher (@sec-consistency-bench,
  @sec-training-law).
- **Locate every gain before adopting it.** When a change improves the
  score, run the test that would reveal a discretization dependence, and ask
  what the change consumes that the physics does not supply. A mechanism that
  cannot be stated is a hypothesis; a gain whose mechanism is the mesh is not
  a gain.
- **Preregister the bar and keep the refuted configurations runnable.**
  Every decision above is made against a bar written before the run. The
  class ISLA ships carries one frame and the options the chapters compare
  against as labeled ablations (the weights-off ablation, the interior
  decodes, both routing forms); the rejected frames (centered and
  similarity-gauge), the constant reference length and the diagnostic
  options are not in the class and their checkpoints do not load, and
  they remain runnable, with their tests, only at the git tag
  `isla-research-full`, so that the price can be re-measured when the data
  or the metric change (@sec-program-status).

The accuracy metric is one number about one discretization of one dataset.
It is necessary and it is not sufficient. A research program that
optimizes it alone will converge on surrogates that know their mesher better
than their physics.

## What a pose prior would buy, and why ISLA does not take it {#sec-pose-prior}

**Every input ISLA takes is a datum of the PDE problem: the geometry, the
boundary data, the material or flow parameters, and the directions the
physics names (an inlet, a load, gravity). The axes of the dataset's
coordinate frame are none of these, and ISLA refuses them even where they
buy accuracy.** A solver never asks which way the dataset's $x$ axis
points. Rotating a whole problem rotates its solution, so a fixed axis
carries no information about the PDE; the only thing it carries is how
the cases were posed. On a dataset where every airfoil has its chord along
$x$, every car points along $x$ and every wing sits in one pose, handing
the model those axes tells it the canonical pose of the training set.
That is exactly the prior GeoTransolver has by construction, because it
reads absolute coordinates, and it is the prior that the pose test of
@sec-pose-contract shows does not survive a change of pose. A model that needs it has stopped
solving the PDE and started remembering where things sit.

That refusal has a price on fixed-pose datasets, and the price is
measured. Because giving ISLA the dataset's axes as extra global directions makes it
ISLA plus GeoTransolver's pose prior, the difference between the frame-free
ISLA and that diagnostic arm is a measurement of how much of
GeoTransolver's lead on a fixed-pose dataset is pose memorization rather
than a better operator. @tbl-pose-prior reports it on every dataset where
it was run, at the reporting protocol, two seeds each. It is a diagnostic
of the baseline's lead. It is not an ISLA configuration, the arms are not
in the recipe's recommended inputs, and no standing in this book uses
them.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-pose-prior
#| output: asis
FAR = J("frame_af_ref_2026-09-26.json"); F3 = J("frame3d_2026-09-26.json"); FW = J("frame_wing_2026-09-26.json")
FPR = J("frame_provided_2026-09-26.json"); FV = J("frame_vol_2026-09-26.json")
FIELDS = [("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
rows = [
    ("AirfRANS interior, 800 airfoils, 100,000 queries, internal geometry: pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity", "inlet + the two laboratory axes",
     " / ".join(f"{FAR['frame_over_internal'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS), " / ".join(f"{FAR['gt_over']['internal'][f]:.2f} → {FAR['gt_over']['frame'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS)),
    ("AirfRANS interior, stored signed-distance field", "inlet + the two laboratory axes",
     " / ".join(f"{FPR['ratios']['over_provided_ref'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS), " / ".join(f"{FPR['comparators']['gt_vol'][f] / FPR['comparators']['provided_ref'][f]:.2f} → {FPR['ratios']['gt_vol_over'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS)),
    ("DrivAerML Surface, 435 cars, 200,000 cells: pressure / wall shear", "inlet + the three body axes",
     " / ".join(f"{F3['ratio_to_r1']['isla_r1_k4'][f]:.2f}" for f in ("pressure_l2", "wss_l2")), f"{F3['gt512_over']['isla_r1']['pressure_l2']:.2f} → {F3['gt512_over']['isla_r1_k4']['pressure_l2']:.2f} (pressure)"),
    ("HiLiftAeroML 35 wings, 200,000 cells: pressure", "far field + the span and up axes",
     f"{FW['fields']['pressure_l2']['frame_over_r1']:.2f}", f"{FW['fields']['pressure_l2']['gt512_over_r1']:.2f} → {FW['fields']['pressure_l2']['gt512_over_frame']:.2f}"),
    ("DrivAerML Volume, 435 cars, stored signed-distance field: pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity", "inlet + the three body axes",
     " / ".join(f"{FV['ratios']['frame_provided_over_provided_ref'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS), " / ".join(f"{FV['ratios']['gt_vol_over_provided_ref'][f]:.2f} → {FV['ratios']['gt_vol_over_frame_provided'][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in FIELDS)),
]
out = "| dataset and readout | axes given to the diagnostic arm | diagnostic ÷ ISLA | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, before → with the pose prior |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
for r in rows:
    out += "| " + " | ".join(r) + " |\n"
print(out)
print(": The pose-prior diagnostic: ISLA at the reference configuration with the dataset's coordinate axes added as global directions, an "
      "input the book rejects, against the frame-free ISLA and the input-matched GeoTransolver (GeoTransolver-512 on the surfaces, "
      "GeoTransolver-volume on the interior tasks), float32 at the reporting protocol, two seeds per arm, seed means. The third column is "
      "the diagnostic arm's error divided by ISLA's (below one: the axes buy accuracy); the last is GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA before and with "
      "the axes (above one favors ISLA). How to read this: the column of gains is the price ISLA pays for refusing the pose prior on a "
      "dataset that never changes pose, and the amount by which the baseline's lead shrinks is the share of that lead that is pose "
      "memorization; it is not a configuration and it is not evidence for ISLA. Data: results/frame_af_ref_2026-09-26.json, "
      "results/frame_provided_2026-09-26.json, results/frame3d_2026-09-26.json, results/frame_wing_2026-09-26.json, "
      "results/frame_vol_2026-09-26.json. {#tbl-pose-prior}")
```

Two readings follow. On AirfRANS the axes close most of the pressure and
eddy-viscosity gap to GeoTransolver-volume, so most of that lead is the
fixed pose of the airfoils: every chord lies along $x$ and every angle of
attack is a rotation of the inlet about a known origin. On the wings the
axes recover about half of the gap at low angles and a quarter at high,
so the pose is part of the wing deficit and the separated regime is the
rest (@sec-de-strata). On the cars the axes buy 5%, the smallest effect,
on the one dataset where ISLA is already at parity with its parameter
match. None of this changes what ISLA is given. Where a plane of the
problem is physical, a ground plane under a car or the symmetry plane of a
half-wing, it is a boundary and belongs in the boundary geometry, not in
the list of directions.
